top_choice_rationale: P002 (B001, Grossman and Helpman) is the best fit to the common criteria of a big question, explanatory power, maturity and attribution. The protection-for-sale framework turned why governments depart from free trade into a tractable equilibrium model, and it produced a structural empirical literature. Credit rests on a sustained two-person partnership that no colleague disputed, and three decades of extension and critique leave no maturity question. Its main weakness is the mixed, specification-dependent empirical record. I read that as contested magnitudes, not as no lasting contribution, and the citation should credit the framework and the research it opened, not confirmed predictions. P001 (B020) is a close second because it changed data use and policy evaluation more visibly. Its unresolved credit boundary (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum, and Redding) cannot be repaired within the credited list, which keeps it just behind. P004 (B019) follows. Its designs are credible, but the magnitude and persistence of the China-shock effects are debated, and its attribution is unsettled across the task-framework strand and the Dorn/Katz question. P003 (B016) ranks next. It has breadth but weaker identification, an unclean split between the Persson-Tabellini and Besley-Persson strands, and some overlap with the 2024 prize. No award is last because several candidates clearly meet the standard for a prize.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile. My frequent co-authors (Bayer, Anwar, Lindquist, Holmlund, Lochner, Bindler) are not credited on any proposal. My labour and crime economics is adjacent to B019, but I have no personal or collaborative tie to its candidates. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
